data.description:
## Description
**What**: Extend /dso:fix-bug Phase G to run after the 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step. On a bug closed with reason="Fixed: ...", a sonnet sub-agent evaluates extraction conditions (not caught by an existing test AND generalizable), performs mandatory pre-extraction redaction of credentials/tokens/keys/PII/internal IDs, requires non-vacuous scope_claim and falsification fields, writes the NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag atomically, falls back to bug_type_slug=unclassified + retro-needs-classification tag when 4911 did not set a slug, logs a SKIP_RECORD comment on every skip, and validates intent_ids_if_applicable against 94ed manifest entries at write time.
**Why**: This is the capture half of the walking-skeleton loop — without it the corpus is never populated.
**Scope**:
- IN: Phase G prompt/logic edits; sonnet extraction evaluation; redaction step; scope_claim/falsification vacuity gate; atomic comment+tag write with rollback; unclassified fallback; SKIP_RECORD audit comment; intent_id write-time validation.
- OUT: retrieval (draft-3); graduation (draft-5/6); lifecycle reopening hook (draft-7).

## Done Definitions

- Phase G extraction executes only after the 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step has run, and reads the bug_type_<slug> tag that step sets ← Satisfies: sc-2
- On a closed-Fixed bug meeting extraction conditions (not caught by an existing test and generalizable pattern) the sonnet step produces a NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment whose missed_signal_summary describes what FAILED to be detected, and on a bug not meeting the conditions it produces a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Credentials, tokens, keys, PII, customer/user identifiers, and internal-only IDs are redacted from all NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE string fields before write; when redaction confidence is insufficient the extraction is skipped and a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason is emitted ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When scope_claim or falsification is vacuous the extraction is skipped and a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason is emitted, matching the SKIP_RECORD shape used by the conditions-not-met and redaction skip paths so every skip leaves an audit comment ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment plus negative-example tag are applied as a single atomic unit that rolls back if either write fails ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When 4911 classification did not set bug_type_<slug>, the record uses bug_type_slug=unclassified and the ticket receives a retro-needs-classification tag; intent_ids_if_applicable values are validated against 94ed manifest entries at write time, with invalid values causing write failure or being dropped with a warning ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Dependency] EXTERNAL BLOCKER: SC2 ordering requires 4911-c7ba's bug-type classification step to set bug_type_<slug>; do not create an in-epic depends_on for 4911 — coordinate via the documented cross-epic dependency.
- [Dependency] EXTERNAL BLOCKER: intent_id validation reads 94ed-f55c manifest entries; the manifest schema is owned by 94ed.
- [Risk] Inverted-polarity: missed_signal_summary must describe what FAILED to be detected, NOT what the test checks — assert polarity explicitly in tests using the canonical contract example.
- [Privacy] Redaction is mandatory pre-write; a fixture bug carrying a token must result in redaction or a skip, never a leaked credential.
- [CrossStory] The NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE and SKIP_RECORD comments must carry a reliable creation timestamp so draft-5's since-last-retro watermark can compare its cursor against them when counting examples_extracted_since_last_retro and examples_skipped_count (SC9(l)); stamp the timestamp at write time on both comment kinds.
- [CrossEpic] 411b auto-created mutation-breach bugs flow through Phase G with no special handling per the epic cross-epic comment.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint orchestrator, I want closed-fixed bugs to be evaluated and recorded as NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comments during /dso:fix-bug Phase G, so that test-miss lessons are captured atomically with privacy redaction and a skip audit trail.
